lanes.D: Data & test infrastructure (docker-compose, synthetic data, mock API)
lanes.C: Core logic (pure functions: guard, compiler, linter, planner, cache)
lanes.H: History, audit, context index (SQLite metadata DB)
lanes.A: Adapters (PostgreSQL first; OpenAPI; Oracle/SQL Server/Elasticsearch later)
lanes.S: Semantic-layer bootstrap pipeline (deterministic stages D*, agentic stages A*)
lanes.M: MCP server and Claude Code plugin

tasks.title: Adopt the skeleton and verify the toolchain
tasks.description: The repo skeleton (pyproject, src layout, conftest, scripts) already exists. Make it a real git repo on branch `main`, create a venv, install `.[dev,pg]`, and make sure `python scripts/check.py` (ruff + mypy + unit tests) is green. Add a GitHub Actions workflow with a matrix of ubuntu-latest and windows-latest, Python 3.11 and 3.13, running scripts/check.py. Check that `python scripts/next_tasks.py status` works from the repo.
acceptance: `git log` shows one initial commit on `main`; .gitignore keeps .venv and data out
`python scripts/check.py` exits 0 on a clean checkout
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` exists with the OS x Python matrix (it cannot be run locally; just be valid YAML)
`python scripts/next_tasks.py ready` lists F02, F03 and others as ready after F01 is marked done
tasks.notes: Do not change the dependency pins in pyproject.toml except to fix a resolution error; note any change in progress/F01.md.

tasks.title: Core domain models (pydantic)
tasks.description: Frozen pydantic v2 models, shared by all lanes, in `mdqm.models`: Capability (tri-state `supported: true|false|unknown`, `detail`, `source: probed|override`), Capabilities (per source), CatalogSnapshot (Table, Column with native + normalized type, Index, ForeignKey, row estimate, comment), Partitioning (strategy range|list|hash|expression|none, key columns or expression, granularity, bounds list), TableStats (mutability counters, row estimate, last analyze), RawQuery (text, dialect, calls?, last_seen?, user?), PlanSummary (partitions_scanned, partitions_total, uses_index, est_rows, est_cost, pruning_proof: proven|unproven|unknown, raw), Limits (timeout_s, max_rows, max_bytes, max_partitions), Fragment (source, dialect, sql|dsl|request, params, tables, exec_ts), ErrorResponse (status='error', code, problem, fix, partitions_if_fixed?, valid_values?, did_you_mean?). Add `mdqm.models.schema.export_json_schemas(dir)` and a stable `snapshot_hash(CatalogSnapshot)`.
acceptance: every model is frozen, `extra='forbid'`, JSON round-trips (`model_validate_json(m.model_dump_json()) == m`)
snapshot_hash is identical for the same content regardless of column/table order in the input
export_json_schemas writes one file per public model and a test asserts the files are valid JSON Schema
ErrorResponse serialises to exactly the shape in docs/DESIGN.md section 'Error shape'

tasks.title: Settings and secret providers
tasks.description: `mdqm.config`: pydantic-settings based `Settings` (server bind, paths for metadata DB / semantic dir / cache dir, model endpoint, SMTP, quiet_windows, limits) loaded from env vars (`MDQM_*`) and an optional `mdqm.yaml`. `SourceConfig` list (name, adapter kind, secret ref, load limits, adapter-specific options). `SecretProvider` Protocol with `EnvSecretProvider` and `FileSecretProvider` (a directory of files, as mounted by Docker/Kubernetes secrets). Secrets are never in YAML, never in repr/logs.
acceptance: a YAML containing a literal password field for a source fails validation with a message pointing to `secret:`
`repr(settings)` and `settings.model_dump_json()` never contain a secret value (use SecretStr)
env overrides file; unknown keys are rejected with the key path in the error
quiet_windows parse with timezone (e.g. Asia/Jerusalem, 21:00-07:00 crossing midnight) and `is_quiet(now)` is tested for edge cases
tasks.notes: Use zoneinfo. On Windows zoneinfo needs the `tzdata` package: add it to dependencies (it is pure Python).

tasks.title: SourceAdapter protocol, plugin registry, conformance kit
tasks.description: Implement the `SourceAdapter` Protocol exactly as in docs/DESIGN.md 'Adapter interface' (required: kind, dialect, probe, extract_catalog, execute, cancel; optional: extract_partitions, explain, mine_queries, mutability_stats which raise `NotSupported`). Registry discovers adapters via entry-point group `mdqm.adapters` (importlib.metadata) and also accepts explicit registration for tests. `mdqm.testing.conformance` provides reusable pytest checks (`run_conformance(adapter_factory)`) that every adapter must pass: probe returns Capabilities, catalog is non-empty, execute respects max_rows and timeout, cancel works, optional methods either work or raise NotSupported (never return garbage).
acceptance: entry-point discovery is tested with importlib.metadata test doubles (no real install needed)
an adapter missing a required method fails registration with a clear error
calling an unimplemented optional method raises `NotSupported` and the probe reports that capability as unsupported
conformance kit is importable from tests of other lanes

tasks.title: FakeAdapter backed by DuckDB for unit tests
tasks.description: A configurable in-memory adapter (DuckDB under the hood, dialect `duckdb`) that other lanes use instead of Docker: load tables from Arrow/Python rows, declare partitioning metadata, declare which optional capabilities exist, count calls (`adapter.calls`), inject latency or failures, and fake `explain()` from declared partitions. It must pass the conformance kit from F04.
acceptance: passes `run_conformance`
can be constructed with and without partition metadata / explain / query history, and the probe reflects that
`execute` enforces max_rows and a (simulated) timeout; `calls` records the fragment SQL

tasks.title: Error taxonomy and structured tool results
tasks.description: Enumerate error codes used by guard/linter/planner/limits (PARTITION_SCAN_ALL, UNKNOWN_TABLE, UNKNOWN_COLUMN, AMBIGUOUS_VALUE, JOIN_NOT_APPROVED, INSERTION_TIME_NO_BOUND, WRITE_BLOCKED, COST_TOO_HIGH, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, TIMEOUT, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, ...) with a helper that builds `ErrorResponse` carrying a concrete `fix`. Every code has a unit test proving the `fix` text is actionable (mentions the exact spec field or value to change).
acceptance: every code has a builder and a test
no error message contains stack traces, SQL with literals from other users, or secrets

tasks.title: docker-compose dev environment with profiles
tasks.description: docker-compose.yml with one service per engine, each behind a profile so an agent starts only what its task needs: `pg` (postgres 16, `-c shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements`, three databases crm/billing/erp created by init SQL plus read-only role `mdqm_ro`), `oracle` (gvenzl/oracle-free slim-faststart), `mssql` (mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server 2022), `es` (elasticsearch 8.x single node, security disabled, 1GB heap), `api` (the mock OpenAPI service from D04, runs as a Python container). Every service has a healthcheck. Ports are bound to 127.0.0.1 on non-default host ports (e.g. 55432) to avoid clashing with local installs. `scripts/dev.py up|down|status <profile...>` wraps docker compose (cross-platform, stdlib only). `scripts/wait_for.py` waits for a TCP port/HTTP URL with timeout.
acceptance: `docker compose config -q` passes with every profile enabled
`python scripts/dev.py up pg` starts Postgres and exits 0 only when healthy; `python scripts/dev.py down` removes volumes
docs/dev-env.md lists memory needs per profile (Oracle + MSSQL + ES together need roughly 10-12 GB; say so) and Windows notes (Docker Desktop with WSL2, Linux containers)
no secret other than throwaway dev passwords, all in .env.example
tasks.test: docker compose --profile pg --profile es --profile mssql --profile oracle --profile api config -q
tasks.notes: If Docker is not available in the sandbox the agent must still produce the files and run only `config -q`; say so in progress/D01.md. Do not tick integration acceptance items you could not run.

tasks.title: Synthetic world generator (seeded, no database needed)
tasks.description: Deterministic generator (use `random.Random(seed)`, not numpy; output must be byte-identical across OSes) of a small organisation, as plain Python rows plus a ground-truth object. Entities: customers (default 2,000; `--small` 200) with a true credit limit; three DATASETS holding the same customers in three storage forms: (1) `crm`: customers(cust_id INT, status 'A'|'C'|'S', credit_limit rounded half-up to 5000), (2) `billing`: accounts(client_no VARCHAR(10) zero-padded e.g. '0000001234', state 'Active'|'Closed'|'Hold', credit_limit RAW unrounded) and usage_events(event_id, client_no, start_time, insertion_time, units, ...), (3) `erp`: customers(cust_no INT, status_code 1|2|3, limit_k = round_half_up(limit/5000)*5000/10) so values are multiples of 500. usage_events: ~50k rows over 8 months, `start_time` is event time, `insertion_time = start_time + lag` where lag is mostly seconds, 1% up to 6 hours, never more than `max_lag` (configurable; an option plants violations for drift tests). Plant: exact .5 boundary limits (2500, 7500, 12500) to expose half-up vs banker's rounding, NULLs, orphan client_no values with no customer, duplicate customer rows in one dataset, a handful of backdated corrections in usage_events (append-rarely), and an `accounts_hist` table with frequent updates (mutable_critical) having `updated_at`. Ground truth (`world.expected`): canonical status per customer, canonical rounded limit, and precomputed answers to the eval questions (e.g. average rounded limit per canonical status, event counts per month, late-arriving rows).
acceptance: same seed gives identical rows on two runs; a different seed gives different rows (test compares a SHA-256 of the serialised world)

invariants: crm limits all multiples of 5000; erp limit_k * 10 equals crm limit for >=99.5% of shared customers (the rest are planted exceptions listed in ground truth); erp values multiples of 500; billing raw has <=5% multiples of 5000
lag distribution: p99 <= max_lag, max <= max_lag unless violations are enabled
boundary rows exist and ground truth uses half-up (2500 -> 5000, 7500 -> 10000)
`python -m mdqm.testing.world --seed 1 --out data/world.json` writes the world and ground truth
tasks.notes: Dataset names (crm/billing/erp) are logical. Tonight's integration tests load all three into three Postgres databases so the cross-source conversion problem is testable with Postgres only. Oracle and SQL Server loaders (D05, D06) later host `billing` and `erp` on the real engines.

tasks.title: PostgreSQL schema + loader (partitioned tables, read-only role)
tasks.description: Loader that creates the schema and loads the world into three Postgres databases: crm (customers), billing (accounts, usage_events, accounts_hist, a small lookup table), erp (customers). Partitioning: `usage_events` RANGE by month on `start_time` (index on start_time, NO index on insertion_time), a second table `usage_by_load` RANGE by month on `insertion_time` (partition key is ingestion time), a HASH-partitioned table (4 partitions), and plain unpartitioned tables with indexes. Create read-only role `mdqm_ro` (SELECT only, `default_transaction_read_only=on`), enable `pg_stat_statements`, run ANALYZE. Loader is idempotent (drop/create) and exposed as `python -m mdqm.testing.loaders.postgres --small`.
acceptance: running the loader twice yields identical row counts
`mdqm_ro` cannot INSERT/UPDATE/DDL (test asserts the error)
catalog queries show 12+ monthly partitions for usage_events and EXPLAIN of `WHERE start_time >= <last 30 days>` touches <=2 partitions while `WHERE insertion_time >= ...` touches all
pg_stat_statements view is readable by `mdqm_ro`
tasks.notes: Prereq: `python scripts/dev.py up pg`.

tasks.title: Mock OpenAPI service for the API adapter
tasks.description: A FastAPI app (test-only) serving two GET endpoints shaped like real internal APIs: `/rates` (filters: currency, date_from, date_to; paginated with `cursor`) and `/customers/{id}/score`. Requires header `X-API-Key`. Returns `X-RateLimit-Remaining`/`Retry-After` and 429 when the budget is exhausted (configurable). `/_stats` returns per-endpoint call counts so tests can prove caching/coalescing avoided calls. Serves its own `/openapi.json`; a copy is checked in as tests/data/specs/fx.yaml (generated by a script, with a test that fails if it drifts). Can run in-process (uvicorn in a thread) via a pytest fixture, or as a container (profile `api`).
acceptance: pytest fixture `mock_api` starts it on an ephemeral port and tears it down
wrong key -> 401, over budget -> 429 with Retry-After, pagination covers all rows exactly once
the checked-in spec equals the live spec (drift test)
tasks.notes: The unit-test conftest disables sockets. This module needs loopback: mark it `@pytest.mark.enable_socket` and allow only 127.0.0.1 (pytest-socket `socket_allow_hosts`).

tasks.title: Oracle loader (billing dataset, interval partitioning)
tasks.description: Load the `billing` dataset into Oracle Free: usage_events partitioned with `PARTITION BY RANGE (start_time) INTERVAL (NUMTOYMINTERVAL(1,'MONTH'))`, read-only user with SELECT on the schema and on V$SQL, index on start_time only. python-oracledb Thin mode (no Oracle client).
acceptance: loader idempotent; row counts equal the world's
read-only user cannot write; can read ALL_PART_TABLES, ALL_PART_KEY_COLUMNS, V$SQL
EXPLAIN PLAN exposes PSTART/PSTOP and a literal date filter shows a numeric (not KEY) range
tasks.notes: Prereq: `python scripts/dev.py up oracle` (slow first start: minutes, ~1 GB image). Mark tests `slow`.

tasks.title: SQL Server loader (erp dataset, partition function/scheme)
tasks.description: Load the `erp` dataset into SQL Server: usage-like table partitioned by month via partition function/scheme, read-only login, Query Store enabled on the database, `VIEW DATABASE STATE` granted to the read-only login. Driver per task A08 (until then: try `mssql-python`, fall back to `pyodbc`).
acceptance: loader idempotent
read-only login cannot write
sys.partition_functions/sys.partition_schemes show the monthly partitions
Query Store views readable by the login
tasks.notes: Prereq: `python scripts/dev.py up mssql`. The SQL Server image needs >=2 GB RAM and does not run natively on ARM Macs; on Windows with WSL2 it works.

tasks.title: Elasticsearch loader (monthly indices, alias, template)
tasks.description: Load usage events into monthly indices `usage-events-YYYY.MM` behind alias `usage-events`, with an index template and explicit mapping (`start_time` date, `insertion_time` date, `client_no` keyword, `units` long). Use plain httpx (no `elasticsearch` Python package: it must work with 8.x and 9.x servers and that client is strictly version coupled).
acceptance: indices and alias exist; document counts match the world
a date-range query on a single month touches one index via index pattern
tasks.notes: Prereq: `python scripts/dev.py up es`.

tasks.title: Golden SQL corpus for miners and translators
tasks.description: Hand-written realistic query corpus, 40+ queries per dialect (postgres, oracle, tsql), in `tests/data/queries/<dialect>.sql` separated by `-- ---`, each preceded by a `-- expect:` JSON comment describing expected extraction: tables, join edges (including conversion joins such as `LPAD(CAST(c.cust_id AS VARCHAR),10,'0') = e.client_no`, `TO_CHAR`, `CAST`), filter columns, time columns, group by, aggregations, rounding expressions (`ROUND(x/5000)*5000`), and which now()-like functions appear. Include ugly cases: CTEs, subqueries, comments, quoted identifiers, Hebrew string literals, dialect specifics (Oracle `SYSDATE`, `ROWNUM`, `FETCH FIRST`; T-SQL `TOP`, `GETDATE()`, `[brackets]`; Postgres `now() - interval`, `::cast`). The test only validates the corpus itself: every statement parses with sqlglot in its dialect and every `expect` block is valid against a pydantic model.
acceptance: 3 files with >=40 statements each; >=10 per dialect contain conversion joins or rounding expressions
every statement parses with `sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read=dialect)`
expect blocks validate against an `ExpectedExtraction` model defined in the test module
tasks.notes: This corpus is the oracle for tasks C01, C02 and S08. Keep each statement short enough to review by eye.

tasks.title: Read-only SQL guard (AST based)
tasks.description: `guard(sql, dialect) -> GuardResult` using sqlglot: allow only a single SELECT / WITH...SELECT / UNION statement. Block DML, DDL, multiple statements, `SELECT ... INTO`, `FOR UPDATE`, `COPY`, `EXEC`, stored-procedure calls, and a configurable denylist of dangerous functions (pg_read_file, pg_sleep, lo_*, dblink, xp_cmdshell, OPENROWSET, DBMS_*, UTL_*, ...). Parse failure is a rejection, never an allow. Run it also on SQL that the server itself compiled.
acceptance: table-driven tests for all three dialects: >=25 allowed and >=40 blocked statements, including comment tricks, `;` smuggling, a CTE wrapping a DML (Postgres data-modifying CTE), and unicode lookalikes
unparseable input is rejected with code WRITE_BLOCKED or PARSE_ERROR, never raises
all statements in tests/data/queries/*.sql are allowed (they are all SELECTs)

tasks.title: exec_ts substitution (now/SYSDATE/GETDATE and friends)
tasks.description: Rewrite, with sqlglot, every non-deterministic time function to an absolute timestamp literal derived from one `exec_ts` per execution: NOW(), CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_DATE, LOCALTIMESTAMP, SYSDATE, SYSTIMESTAMP, GETDATE(), GETUTCDATE(), SYSDATETIME(), and interval arithmetic on them (`now() - interval '7 days'` -> literal). Return the rewritten SQL plus a list of Replacement(original, replaced_with, position) for audit. Also implement the Elasticsearch date-math equivalent (`now-7d/d`) on a Query DSL dict. Timezone: exec_ts is UTC-aware; the literal is rendered in the source's session timezone, passed as an argument (default UTC). Two modes: `frozen` (use the stored exec_ts of a past run) and `relative` (use now).
acceptance: property test: rewriting twice is a no-op; rewritten SQL contains none of the function names
all now-like calls in tests/data/queries/*.sql are replaced; replacements match the `expect` blocks
DST edge: a Jerusalem session timezone around the late-October change renders the correct literal
ES: `now-7d/d` with exec_ts=2026-11-25T10:00Z becomes the absolute range bound, rounding semantics of `/d` respected

tasks.title: Query spec models and duration parser
tasks.description: Pydantic models for the structured query spec (see docs/DESIGN.md 'Query spec'): from, select (column names, measures with agg, aliases), filters (equality, in, range, contains; values may be Hebrew/English labels), time ({mode: events_in_range, last|from/to} or {mode: new_since, since}), group_by, order_by, limit, joins (by approved-join name only), dry_run, fresh. Duration parser for `30d`, `3mo`, `1y`, `6h`, ISO-8601 durations; calendar months handled correctly. Export a JSON Schema with enums filled in at runtime from the semantic layer (function `spec_schema(semantic)`). examples/query_specs.json already holds the canonical examples; the tests must load and validate every one.
acceptance: all examples in examples/query_specs.json validate; the ones under `invalid` fail with the listed error paths
durations: `1mo` from 2026-01-31 is handled deterministically and the choice is documented in the test
the JSON Schema is usable as an OpenAI-compatible `response_format` (valid, no unsupported keywords, no `$ref` cycles)

tasks.title: Semantic layer models and YAML loader (generated + curated)
tasks.description: Models and loader for the YAML in examples/semantic_example.yaml: version, sources, defaults (cache, quiet_windows), value_maps, measures (canonical + per-source normalize templates), tables (key, default_window, partitioning, time_columns with role/indexed/use_by_default/lag, mutability class + status, cache override), approved_joins (with cardinality and usage). Two directories: `generated/` (machine written) and `curated/` (human written, wins on conflict, merged per key). Every item can carry `provenance` (detected_by, evidence, match_rate, approved_by, approved_at). The loader returns an immutable `SemanticLayer` with a content hash (`version_hash`) that goes into cache keys and audit. Validation errors name the file, YAML path and line (ruamel keeps line info). A writer API updates generated files without touching curated ones and preserves comments in curated files on round-trip.
acceptance: the example YAML loads; mutation of a loaded layer is impossible (frozen)
curated overrides generated per key, and removing a curated key restores the generated value
version_hash changes when any semantic content changes and does not change on comment/whitespace edits
a typo in a field name gives an error with file, line and path
unknown mutability class is rejected; `unknown` is accepted and treated conservatively

tasks.title: Value-map resolver (multilingual categorical values)
tasks.description: Given a value_map and any user-supplied label (Hebrew, English, source code like 'A' or 'Hold'), resolve to the canonical value. Normalise with NFKC, case-fold, strip, collapse whitespace, remove Hebrew niqqud and punctuation variants (geresh/gershayim, quotes, maqaf). Ambiguous or unknown input returns a structured result carrying the valid canonical values and the closest matches (`did_you_mean`, difflib), never a guess. Reverse mapping: canonical -> per-source code(s) for compiling filters (`status = 'A'` on crm, `'Active'` on billing, `1` on erp).
acceptance: table-driven tests in Hebrew and English: the Hebrew word for active, ' Active ', 'active' and the code 'A' all resolve to `active` where the map says so
an input that matches two canonical values through synonyms returns AMBIGUOUS_VALUE, not the first match
reverse mapping returns the right per-source literal and type (string vs int)
values with niqqud or gershayim variants resolve identically to their plain form

tasks.title: Measure normalisation and rounding semantics
tasks.description: Per-source normalisation templates (`{col}`, `ROUND({col} / 5000) * 5000`, `{col} * 10`) are parsed with sqlglot and validated against an allowlist (arithmetic, ROUND/FLOOR/CEIL, CAST, no subqueries, no unknown functions). Render per dialect. Rounding mode is part of the canonical definition (`half_up` | `half_even`); implement it explicitly (do NOT rely on engine defaults or Python's round(), which is banker's). Add a sanity check for results: values must be multiples of the canonical rounding (`to`); it reports violations rather than raising.
acceptance: on DuckDB, the three forms of the credit_limit measure from the D02 world normalise to the same canonical value for >=99.5% of shared customers
boundary values 2500 and 7500 round up (half_up) in the rendered SQL for postgres, oracle, tsql dialects (assert the SQL text AND evaluate on DuckDB)
a template with a subquery or unknown function is rejected at load time with the template path
sanity check flags a non-multiple of 5000 in a normalised result and counts it

tasks.title: Time planner (event time vs insertion time, derived bound)
tasks.description: Pure function turning a spec `time` intent plus a table's time_columns metadata into predicates (sqlglot expressions) and notes: `events_in_range` -> range on the column marked use_by_default (event time, indexed). `new_since X` -> `insertion_time >= X` PLUS derived bound `start_time >= X - max_lag` (the original predicate stays so late arrivals are not lost). If lag is unknown or lag verification failed, do not derive: require a narrow range or return INSERTION_TIME_NO_BOUND with a fix. A filter that touches the last `max_lag` window gets note `partial_data_possible`. Also handle 'known as of T' (insertion_time <= T plus event range) and the case where the partition key is insertion time (event range [X,Y) -> insertion range [X+min_lag, Y+max_lag)).
acceptance: unit tests reproduce the SQL from docs/DESIGN.md 'Time columns' (insertion_time >= 14:00 gives start_time >= 08:00 with a 6h lag)
unknown lag + new_since without a bound yields INSERTION_TIME_NO_BOUND with a fix naming the spec field
property test: for worlds with lag <= max_lag, results with and without the derived bound are identical (D02 world + DuckDB)
partition-key = insertion time case produces the widened range and a test shows no row is lost on the synthetic data

tasks.title: Partition planner (static): require key filter, rewrite, estimate
tasks.description: Given Partitioning metadata and the predicates of a fragment: detect whether the partition key is filtered; if not, inject the table's `default_window` or reject (PARTITION_SCAN_ALL with a `partitions_if_fixed` estimate) depending on `require_key_filter`. Rewrite functions/casts on the key (`CAST(start_time AS DATE) = ...`, `TRUNC(start_time)`, `date_trunc('month', start_time) = ...`) into half-open ranges on the raw column. Estimate partitions touched from declared bounds. Hash partitions: filter must be on the key itself. Expression-keyed: prune only when the predicate matches the expression, else flag needs-human-approval. Provide `align_to_partitions(range) -> list[Range]` used by the cache.
acceptance: table-driven tests per strategy (range-monthly, list, hash, expression, none)
function-on-key rewrite is semantically equal: evaluate before/after on DuckDB with the synthetic data and compare results
error carries a `partitions_if_fixed: '2 of 60'` style estimate
alignment splits a 70-day range into month-aligned segments with correct half-open bounds

tasks.title: Single-source compiler: spec to SQL (Postgres first)
tasks.description: Compile a validated spec for ONE source into SQL via the sqlglot AST: select/measure normalisation (C06), filters with value-map resolution (C05), time predicates (C07), partition handling (C08), LIMIT injection from limits, exec_ts substitution (C02), and a final guard pass (C01). Output a `Fragment`. Golden-file tests in tests/data/golden/*.sql (update with `--update-golden`). Dialect is a parameter; Postgres is the target tonight.
acceptance: every `valid` example from examples/query_specs.json compiles to committed golden SQL for postgres (tests may extend a test semantic layer under tests/data/semantic/ with measures the example YAML lacks, e.g. event_count and month)
every compiled fragment passes the guard and contains no now-like function
an unapproved join in the spec produces JOIN_NOT_APPROVED with the approved join's full ON clause in `fix`
compile is deterministic (same inputs, byte-identical SQL)

tasks.title: Compiler dialect golden tests: Oracle and T-SQL
tasks.description: Extend golden coverage to dialect `oracle` (FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY, TO_TIMESTAMP literals, quoting) and `tsql` (TOP / OFFSET FETCH, brackets, datetime2 literals). Use `unsupported_level=RAISE` so unsupported constructs fail loudly. Fix compiler issues found; do not special-case the tests.
acceptance: the same specs as C09 compile to committed golden SQL for oracle and tsql
an intentionally unsupported construct raises a typed error, not silent best-effort SQL
all outputs parse back with sqlglot in their dialect

tasks.title: Linter: auto-fixes and errors with an exact fix
tasks.description: Rule registry over the spec (primary) and raw SQL (emergency path; goes through the AST). Auto-fix only meaning-preserving cases and report each in `applied_fixes`: missing LIMIT, categorical label -> canonical, raw column that has a measure -> measure, insertion_time filter -> derived bound, function on partition key -> raw range, now() -> exec_ts. Return an `ErrorResponse` with a concrete `fix` for everything else: unknown table/column (with did-you-mean), unapproved join (with the approved ON), ambiguous value (with valid values), no filter on partition key, DML/DDL. Each rule is a small class with an id, severity, autofix flag, and tests with before/after specs.
acceptance: at least 12 rules, each with an auto-fix test or an error test asserting the `fix` text
a fix that would change meaning is never applied silently (tests: ambiguous value, unapproved join)
linting is idempotent: lint(lint(x).fixed) == lint(x).fixed
a Hebrew label for 'active' in a filter is rewritten to the canonical value and listed in applied_fixes

tasks.title: Cache freshness rule (pure function)
tasks.description: `is_fresh(age, range_from, range_to, theta=0.01, min_ttl=30s, max_ttl=7d, mutability)`: fresh iff `age <= max(min_ttl, theta * (range_to - range_from))` and `age <= max_ttl`. Mutability policy: append_only and append_rarely use the rule; mutable_critical and unknown are never served from cache (or use a per-table short TTL if configured). A closed (sealed) partition segment is bounded only by max_ttl and the nightly verification flag. Worked example from the design: a 1-year pull from yesterday is fresh, a 1-week pull from yesterday is stale.
acceptance: hypothesis property tests: monotonic in age; a wider range is never less fresh; mutable_critical never fresh
unit tests for the 1 year vs 1 week example and the min_ttl floor
documented behaviour at exact boundaries (<= vs <)

tasks.title: Single-flight coalescing for identical concurrent calls
tasks.description: Async helper: concurrent callers with the same key share one in-flight execution and one result (or one exception); cancelling one caller must not cancel the others; the key is removed afterwards.
acceptance: 100 concurrent identical calls execute the function exactly once
an exception propagates to all waiters and the next call retries
cancelling one waiter does not cancel the shared work for the rest

tasks.title: Segment cache on DuckDB (partition aligned, tail refresh)
tasks.description: Store query results as segments keyed by (source, table, fragment-hash without time range, semantic version_hash, partition-aligned range). Lookup returns hit / stale / miss per segment with `fetched_at` and age. Tail refresh: for append tables with a unique key, fetch only `insertion_time >= fetched_at` (with the derived bound) and merge by key; otherwise refetch the segment. Eviction by max_ttl and total size; DuckDB `memory_limit` and a spill directory come from Settings. In-memory DuckDB for tests, file-backed in production. No DuckDB extensions (they need internet to install).
acceptance: a repeated identical request is served with zero adapter calls (assert via FakeAdapter.calls)
a sealed past month is a hit; the current month is a tail refresh that fetches only new rows and merging dedupes by key
mutable_critical and unknown tables never populate the cache
changing the semantic version_hash invalidates affected segments

tasks.title: Governor: concurrency, quotas, timeouts, result handles
tasks.description: Per-source semaphores, per-user concurrency and rate quota (token bucket), global max concurrent queries, row/byte caps, per-call timeout with cancellation, circuit breaker for a failing source. Result store: `ResultHandle` (opaque id, TTL, owner) holding the full Arrow result on disk/in memory; `get_more(handle, offset, limit)` only for the owner. Defaults from docs/DESIGN.md: 8 concurrent in the server, 2 per user, 2-3 per source.
acceptance: load test with 50 concurrent fake queries never exceeds the configured per-source concurrency (assert max observed)
user A cannot read user B's handle
timeouts cancel the adapter call and release the semaphore
quota exceeded returns QUOTA_EXCEEDED with the reset time in `fix`

tasks.title: Result summariser (summary + sample + handle, token budget)
tasks.description: Turn an Arrow table into: row count, column stats (min/max/nulls/distinct for the top columns), a small sample, and a handle. Token estimation without extra dependencies (conservative heuristic that handles Hebrew: roughly chars/2.5 for Hebrew-heavy text, chars/4 for ASCII). Default response budget well below 10,000 tokens; hard cap 25,000.
acceptance: a 10-million-row table summarises under the budget in under 1 second
Hebrew-heavy output is counted more conservatively than ASCII in a test
the summary never includes more than `sample_rows` rows

tasks.title: Federated executor (fragments per source, DuckDB join, quality report)
tasks.description: Split a multi-source spec into per-source fragments (max filter pushdown), run them through the governor and cache, register the Arrow results in DuckDB and run the join, normalisation and aggregation locally. Produce a quality report: rows dropped by each join (left key with no match), unmapped categorical values, normalisation sanity violations, per-fragment `fetched_at`. Caps per fragment (rows, bytes); exceeding one returns COST_TOO_HIGH with a `fix` that narrows the filter.
acceptance: with 3 FakeAdapters holding crm/billing/erp from the D02 world, the cross-source `avg credit_limit_r5000 by customer_status` equals the ground truth exactly
the join report lists the planted orphan client_no rows (count matches ground truth)
a fragment over its row cap is rejected before the join with COST_TOO_HIGH
a second identical call performs zero adapter calls (cache) and reports freshness per segment

tasks.title: Column quality, categorical distributions and DuckDB collection
tasks.description: Per column: share of NULL, numeric 0, '' and whitespace-only values, distinct count, min/max for numeric and time. A column is categorical when its distinct count is low or a small share of the rows. Distributions keep the top values plus an 'other' tail, per partition or time bucket, so two readings show drift. DuckDB unit tests measure a table exactly and through a repeatable reservoir sample that records the sample size. False is not zero and the string '0' is not numeric zero.
acceptance: shares of a planted column match the inserted NULL, 0, '' and whitespace counts
a sample records method=sample and the number of rows actually returned
per-bucket distributions differ when the planted months differ
an empty column reports no share rather than zero

tasks.title: Associations, category gate and result-size estimate
tasks.description: Candidate pairs are same-table, low-cardinality X first, and columns co-used in mined queries ahead of the rest, capped. Cramér's V and mutual information for categorical pairs; per-category NULL/0/'' rates and mean/quantiles for a numeric Y. A filter on a categorical value that never occurs is a hard error (VALUE_NOT_IN_DATA) with the closest real values and their frequencies (case, whitespace, Hebrew, transliteration, dictionary synonyms). Stale stats (unprofiled partition, sample, or a non-empty tail) verify with a bounded lookup before rejecting; a lookup that cannot run does not reject. Result size is table rows times filter selectivity, and an unaggregated estimate over the block is COST_TOO_HIGH.
acceptance: Cramér's V is 0 for an independent pair and 1 for a determined pair
a fresh complete distribution rejects a typo without calling the probe, and the fix contains the frequency
a Hebrew synonym of a stored code is allowed
an unprofiled partition calls the probe: found allows, absent rejects, unknown does not reject
co-used column pairs sort ahead of unused ones

tasks.title: SQLite metadata DB with migrations and FTS5 check
tasks.description: Thin SQLite layer (stdlib sqlite3, WAL mode, one writer lock, connection per thread) with numbered SQL migrations applied at startup and recorded in a table. `fts5_available()` check used by the probe; if missing, fail with a clear error naming the Python build. Later tasks add their tables through new migrations.
acceptance: a fresh DB gets all migrations; a second start is a no-op
a migration that fails rolls back and leaves the previous version intact
FTS5 smoke test creates a virtual table and queries it; absence is reported, not crashed

tasks.title: Audit log (append-only, hash chained)
tasks.description: Append-only audit table: user, tool, semantic version_hash, sources touched, row counts, blocked attempts, outcome, timestamp, and `prev_hash`/`hash` chain. `verify_chain()` detects any edit or deletion. Retention purge (default 365 days) removes only whole prefixes and writes a checkpoint hash so verification still works. No user data literals in audit rows beyond what the history already stores.
acceptance: tampering with a row (UPDATE in a test) makes verify_chain fail at the right id
purge keeps the chain verifiable
CLI: `mdqm audit verify` exits 0/1 accordingly

tasks.title: Query history with frozen and relative re-run
tasks.description: Store per run: user, spec or original SQL, SQL with frozen exec_ts, per-source fragments, applied_fixes, plan summary, cache/freshness info, duration, errors. `rerun(id, mode='frozen'|'relative')`: frozen reuses the stored exec_ts, relative substitutes a new one. Text search over history via FTS5. Retention purge (365 days default).
acceptance: frozen rerun produces byte-identical fragments; relative differs only in timestamps
history search finds a past query by Hebrew or English words from its spec
purge removes only expired rows

tasks.title: Context index: FTS5 over the semantic layer (he + en, synonyms)
tasks.description: Index every table, column, measure, value (canonical + synonyms), approved join, and approved example query as a document with fields. FTS5 with `unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`, prefix search, bm25 weights per field. Synonyms are expanded on BOTH the index and the query side. Hebrew has no good offline stemmer: use light prefix stripping for the common one-letter prefixes as an additional query variant, tested. Log queries with zero hits to a table for the data team. Rebuild is incremental by semantic version_hash.
acceptance: table-driven Hebrew/English queries hit the right table (the Hebrew phrase for 'credit limit' and the English one both find credit_limit)
a Hebrew definite-article form ('the customers') finds 'customer' through prefix variants; the test also shows a known miss is logged to empty_searches
rebuild with an unchanged version_hash does no work

tasks.title: Context Pack builder (token budgeted, deterministic)
tasks.description: Given free text (a question or prompt) build the Context Pack automatically injected into answers, errors and the client hook: the top tables, relevant columns with the preferred time column and partition key, value mappings for categorical columns that match, approved joins ordered by usage, and 1-3 approved example specs. Default budget 1,500 tokens (configurable, scales with the model context probed), deterministic ordering, relevance threshold below which an EMPTY pack is returned (so non-data prompts add nothing). Format is compact text/JSON that a weak model can follow; no prose essays.
acceptance: same input and semantic version gives byte-identical output
budget is respected for Hebrew and English (use the C16 estimator or a local heuristic)
a prompt about the weather returns an empty pack; a prompt about credit limits by status returns the credit_limit measure, the status value map, the approved join, and an example spec
the pack includes the `use_by_default` time column and partition key for each table

tasks.title: Metadata store for column, category, association and partition statistics
tasks.description: Append-only statistics tables in the metadata database: column quality, categorical buckets (payload JSON, so a Hebrew value round-trips), associations and partition extents. Each row has collected_at and method. Readers return the newest capture per column or partition. Not part of the semantic layer, so a nightly refresh does not change the version hash.
acceptance: a collected pass round-trips: quality, per-bucket distributions, one association and one extent
a second capture of the same column does not delete the first; latest() returns the newer one
tasks.notes: The second acceptance is the store's query (MAX collected_at). A unit test that writes one capture is enough to lock the schema; a second write is covered by the same reader.

tasks.title: Capability probe framework and capabilities.yaml
tasks.description: Runs each adapter's probe with per-feature timeouts, records tri-state capability with the error detail, merges `overrides.yaml` (admin wins), writes `generated/capabilities.yaml`, and diffs against the previous run. Also probes the metadata store (FTS5 via a callable hook; H01 plugs in later). CLI: `mdqm probe [--source NAME]`. Re-runnable at any time; read-only against sources.
acceptance: with FakeAdapters in 3 configurations the file matches golden YAML
a probe feature that raises or times out becomes `unknown` with detail, never crashes the run
an override flips a feature and survives re-probe; the diff reports `changed: [...]`

tasks.title: PostgreSQL adapter: connect, catalog, execute, cancel
tasks.description: psycopg3 + psycopg_pool. Every connection: `SET SESSION CHARACTERISTICS AS TRANSACTION READ ONLY`, `statement_timeout`, `application_name = mdqm:<user>` (tags queries at the source). extract_catalog from information_schema/pg_catalog (columns, types, PKs, FKs, indexes, comments, row estimates from reltuples). execute streams server-side cursor batches into Arrow with row/byte caps; cancel via psycopg cancel / `pg_cancel_backend`. Register as entry point `postgresql` in pyproject. Pass the conformance kit.
acceptance: passes `run_conformance` against the compose Postgres (crm, billing, erp databases)
a write sent through `execute` is rejected by the server even if the guard is bypassed (test connects with the guard disabled)
a 1s timeout on `pg_sleep` is enforced and the connection returns to the pool healthy
catalog of billing lists usage_events with indexes: start_time indexed, insertion_time not
tasks.notes: Prereq: `python scripts/dev.py up pg` and `python -m mdqm.testing.loaders.postgres --small`.

tasks.title: PostgreSQL: partitions extraction and EXPLAIN pruning proof
tasks.description: extract_partitions via pg_partitioned_table/pg_get_partkeydef/pg_inherits (strategy, key, bounds). explain: `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)` without ANALYZE, parse the plan tree, count scanned partition leaves vs total, report `proven` only for plan-time pruning and `unproven` when parameters would defer it, and report index use. Parsing is a pure function tested on canned JSON plans stored in tests/data/plans/.
acceptance: unit tests parse >=6 canned plans (pruned, unpruned, parameterised, nested loop, index scan, seq scan)
integration: `WHERE start_time >= now()-30d` reports <=2 of 12+ partitions `proven`; a filter on insertion_time reports all partitions
the planner (C08) consumes the result and rejects a plan that exceeds `max_partitions_scanned` with PARTITION_SCAN_ALL
tasks.notes: Integration check: python -m pytest tests/integration/test_pg_partitions.py --require-services -q

tasks.title: PostgreSQL: query mining source and mutability stats
tasks.description: mine_queries from `pg_stat_statements` (query text, calls, mean time) with a watermark; returns RawQuery list. mutability_stats from pg_stat_user_tables (n_tup_ins/upd/del/hot_upd, n_mod_since_analyze, last_autovacuum) deltas between two readings. If the extension is not loaded or not readable the capability is `unsupported`, not an error.
acceptance: with pg_stat_statements enabled the miner returns the queries a test just ran
counters distinguish usage_events (inserts only, few corrections) from accounts_hist (many updates)
extension missing -> probe says unsupported and the pipeline falls back (test with a database where it is not created)

tasks.title: Token-bucket rate limiter shared across API sources
tasks.description: Async token bucket with a shared pool across several sources (`shared_pool: true`), per-source sub-limits, honour `Retry-After`, and jitter. Time source injectable so tests do not sleep.
acceptance: with a fake clock, 100 requests at rps=2 take 50s of fake time
two sources sharing a pool never exceed the pool total
a 429 with Retry-After pauses all members of the pool

tasks.title: OpenAPI adapter (GET only) with virtual tables
tasks.description: Parse an OpenAPI 3.x spec with a small in-house reader (no heavy dependency): each GET collection endpoint becomes a virtual table; query parameters are its 'indexes' (filterable columns), the response schema gives columns; pagination styles cursor/offset/page detected from parameters. API key from the secret provider, never logged. execute turns a Fragment into calls via httpx with pagination, rate limiter (A05), single-flight (C13), TTL cache for identical calls. Only GET is ever issued (assert at the transport layer). Pass the conformance kit.
acceptance: against the mock API: the table catalog matches the spec; a filtered fetch returns exactly the expected rows across pages
a second identical request makes zero HTTP calls (check `/_stats`)
POST/PUT in the spec are ignored; a code path that tries them raises
missing/invalid key gives SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE with a `fix` mentioning the secret name, not the key
tasks.notes: Needs loopback sockets for the mock API (see D04 note).

tasks.title: Oracle adapter
tasks.description: python-oracledb Thin mode. Probe version/edition, catalog (ALL_TAB_COLUMNS, constraints, indexes), partitions (ALL_PART_TABLES, ALL_PART_KEY_COLUMNS, ALL_TAB_PARTITIONS), explain via EXPLAIN PLAN + DBMS_XPLAN (document what a read-only account needs; PSTART/PSTOP numeric = proven, KEY = unproven), V$SQL mining when readable, ALL_TAB_MODIFICATIONS counters. Read-only session. Pass the conformance kit.
acceptance: passes `run_conformance`
pruning proof for a literal date filter is `proven`; a bind-variable filter is `unproven`
V$SQL not readable -> capability unsupported, no crash

tasks.title: SQL Server adapter (includes driver spike)
tasks.description: Start with a one-page driver spike (docs/mssql-driver.md): mssql-python vs pymssql vs pyodbc on Windows, Linux, macOS: wheel availability, need for an ODBC driver, TLS, read-only intent, cancellation. Pick one default and keep the others as optional extras. Then: probe, catalog (sys.* views), partitions (sys.partition_functions/schemes), explain via SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON (count partitions in the plan XML; the format is unverified, so verify it empirically and write the finding down), Query Store mining.
acceptance: docs/mssql-driver.md has a table of findings with versions tested
passes `run_conformance`
Query Store capability detected and used when present

tasks.title: Elasticsearch adapter (httpx, DSL pushdown, ES|QL when present)
tasks.description: Pure httpx REST client. Probe: version, which of ES|QL / SQL API / Query DSL work (Query DSL always). Catalog from _mapping and aliases/data streams/ILM templates (treat each index family as one table). Compile a spec to Query DSL (range on date, term filters, aggregations). Index selection by narrow date pattern, never a wildcard over everything. now-style date math handled by C02. Slow logs for mining only if enabled. No EXPLAIN: report `pruning_proof: unknown` and enforce an index-count cap.
acceptance: passes `run_conformance`
a one-month query touches exactly one monthly index
ES|QL used when available, DSL otherwise (test both paths with a stubbed probe)

tasks.title: Bootstrap pipeline framework (idempotent stages, quiet windows)
tasks.description: Stage interface (`name`, `inputs_hash`, `run(ctx)`), runner that skips a stage when its input hash is unchanged, records runs in SQLite, writes only to `generated/`, honours `quiet_windows` for heavy stages (refuses to run outside the window unless `--force`), per-source concurrency 1-2, abort if source latency rises. CLI: `mdqm bootstrap run [--stage D5] [--source X] [--force]`.
acceptance: unchanged inputs skip the stage (and skip any model call)
a heavy stage outside the quiet window is refused with the next window start in the message
a crash mid-stage leaves generated/ unchanged (write to temp, atomic rename)
curated/ is never written by the pipeline (test asserts file mtimes)

tasks.title: Stages D1+D2: catalog and partitions into generated YAML
tasks.description: Convert CatalogSnapshot + Partitioning for each source into the `tables:` section of `generated/<source>.yaml` (keys, indexes, partitioning, default time column guess by index + name heuristics, `mutability: unknown`). Works from any adapter (tested with FakeAdapter; in E03 also with Postgres).
acceptance: golden YAML for FakeAdapter sources
a table without PK/FK info still appears with `key: unknown`
re-run with no catalog change produces byte-identical output

tasks.title: Stage D4: OpenAPI spec to table skeleton
tasks.description: From the API adapter's virtual catalog write table skeletons: filterable params, pagination, auth header name, rate-limit headers seen.
acceptance: golden YAML for the mock API spec
unknown/unsupported endpoints are listed under `skipped` with a reason

tasks.title: Stage D5: profiling (stats first, then sampling)
tasks.description: Per column: null rate, distinct count (estimated when large), min/max, top-N values with counts, string format patterns (regex classes, zero-padded digits), numeric granularity (largest g such that all non-null values are multiples of g; report 5000, 500, 1 ...) and the share that fits. Order: catalog statistics, then source-side sample (TABLESAMPLE or equivalent), with timeout and row cap; only in quiet windows. Output feeds D7/D8 and the A-stages as a fact sheet.
acceptance: on the synthetic world: crm credit_limit granularity 5000 (100%), erp limit_k granularity 500, billing raw granularity 1 with <=5% multiples of 5000
client_no is detected as zero-padded 10-digit strings
profiling a table over the row cap uses a sample and says so in the fact sheet
no query is issued outside quiet windows unless --force (test with FakeAdapter.calls)

tasks.title: Stage D6: mutability classification and lag measurement
tasks.description: Classify each table append_only / append_rarely / mutable_critical / unknown from counters (A04), `updated_at`-like columns, and a checksum over a sample of old rows compared across runs. Conservative: any evidence of updates in old rows never classifies as append_only. Measure lag between insertion_time and event time (p50, p99, max) for tables that have both; emit `lag: {min, max, verify: nightly}` with max rounded up with margin. Nightly verification re-measures and flags `lag_violated`.
acceptance: on the synthetic world: usage_events = append_rarely, accounts_hist = mutable_critical, the lookup table = append_only
measured max lag <= configured; with planted violations `lag_violated` is raised
an unclassifiable table stays `unknown`

tasks.title: Stage D8: conversion detection (scale, rounding, order of operations)
tasks.description: Given two columns from two sources joined on an entity key (sample pairs as Arrow), search a small hypothesis space: identity, scale by k in {0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 10, 100, 1000}, round-to-g with g from D5 granularity and common values, round-then-scale and scale-then-round, with rounding mode half_up/half_even. Score by match rate on the pairs; report best hypothesis, runner-ups, match rate, and COUNTER-EXAMPLES (rows that do not fit). Accept automatically only above a threshold; everything else becomes a proposal needing human approval. Never invents a formula outside the hypothesis space. Extra hypotheses may come from mining hints (S08) when available.
acceptance: on the synthetic world the detector recovers: crm vs billing -> `ROUND(x/5000)*5000` half_up (match >=99.5%); crm vs erp -> `x*10` after rounding; the planted exceptions are reported as counter-examples
boundary rows (2500, 7500) discriminate half_up from half_even and the detector picks half_up
two unrelated columns yield `no_hypothesis` instead of a weak match
output is a `MeasureProposal` with evidence, ready for the review queue (S12)

tasks.title: Stage D7: join candidates (names, types, containment, format conversion)
tasks.description: Candidate pairs by name similarity (cust_id vs client_no vs cust_no), type, value containment and uniqueness ratio, with detection of FORMAT conversions between the two sides (int vs zero-padded string, prefix, case) emitting the conversion expression as a hypothesis for validation. A declared FK with full containment is auto-approvable; everything else is a proposal.
acceptance: recovers crm.customers.cust_id <-> billing.accounts.client_no with LPAD to 10 zeros, and cust_id <-> erp cust_no (identity)
reports containment ratio and the count of orphan keys (matches the planted orphans)
false positives: two unrelated integer columns with overlapping ranges are not proposed above the threshold

tasks.title: Stage D9: deterministic mining of past queries
tasks.description: From a RawQuery list: parse with sqlglot in the right dialect (failures counted and reported, never fatal), normalise (strip literals, replace now-like with a marker, uppercase keywords, canonical alias handling) and hash the AST into a fingerprint; extract tables, join edges (including conversion expressions such as LPAD/CAST/TO_CHAR), filter columns, time columns used, GROUP BY, aggregations, and rounding/scale expressions; upsert counts per fingerprint (calls, distinct users, first/last seen) in SQLite with a per-source watermark. Ranking score = a*log(count) + b*0.5^(age/half_life) + c*distinct_users with configurable constants. No model involved.
acceptance: extraction on tests/data/queries/*.sql equals the `expect` blocks (>=95% of statements exactly; failures listed in the test output)
two queries differing only in literals and whitespace share a fingerprint; a different join does not
re-ingesting the same queries is idempotent; the watermark advances
conversion expressions (LPAD join, ROUND(x/5000)*5000) are surfaced as typed `ConversionHint`s consumable by S06/S07 as extra hypotheses

tasks.title: Stage D10: schema drift detection
tasks.description: Diff two CatalogSnapshots and classify each change: breaking (dropped/renamed column, type change, partition key change, index dropped on a default time column) vs non-breaking (new column, new partition, new index). Map each breaking change to the semantic YAML entries that reference it. Breaking changes produce an immediate admin notification payload (not waiting for the weekly digest).
acceptance: table-driven diff tests for 12+ change kinds
a dropped column used by a measure lists that measure
a new monthly partition is non-breaking; a partition-key change is breaking

tasks.title: Model client: OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint with closed JSON output
tasks.description: Minimal httpx client for an OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint (base URL, model name, API key from the secret provider; no vendor SDK). `structured(prompt, schema: type[BaseModel])`: ask for JSON constrained by `response_format` json_schema if the probe says it is supported, otherwise instruct and validate in code; up to 2 retries sending the validation error back; temperature 0; prompt template version recorded; response cached by input hash (SQLite or file) so re-runs cost nothing. Include `FakeLLM` for tests. Probe function measures: reachable, tool calling, json_schema support, context window if exposed.
acceptance: a stubbed server (httpx MockTransport) returning invalid JSON then valid JSON succeeds on retry 1 and records both attempts
a cached call performs no second HTTP request
no API key in logs or exceptions
the probe result is a Capabilities entry `model_endpoint` with `structured_output: true|false|unknown`
tasks.notes: We do not know the real on-prem endpoint's compatibility; do not assume more than chat completions. Everything else is probed.

tasks.title: Agentic stages A1+A2: names, descriptions, synonyms (he + en)
tasks.description: For ONE table or column per call, give the model the fact sheet (D1/D5 output) and ask for closed JSON: Hebrew + English display names, one-sentence descriptions, synonyms. Validators: referenced columns exist, language matches field, length limits, no collision with an existing term, no copied example values that look like personal data. Confidence and evidence are computed from validators and a second run with shuffled order (disagreement lowers confidence), NOT from model self-report. Output proposals only (no YAML written).
acceptance: with FakeLLM scripted answers, valid proposals pass and are stored with computed confidence
a proposal naming a nonexistent column is rejected and counted
disagreement between two runs lowers confidence deterministically
temperature 0, prompt version and model name are stored with each proposal

tasks.title: Review queue and approval to curated YAML
tasks.description: Proposal store (SQLite): stable id from content hash, kind (name, synonym, value_map, measure, join, mutability, ...), evidence, confidence, status (pending, approved, rejected, never_ask), who/when. Rejected items are remembered (negative memory) and not re-proposed unless the evidence changes. Approving writes a minimal patch into `curated/*.yaml` with provenance (approved_by, at) and keeps comments; `mdqm review export-patch` writes the same change as a git-friendly diff for the PR flow. Bulk approval of high-confidence items counts as one question.
acceptance: approve -> curated YAML contains the item with provenance and the loader (C04) accepts it
a rejected proposal is not resurfaced on the next run with identical evidence, and is resurfaced if the evidence changes
export-patch output applies cleanly with `git apply` (test in a temp repo)

tasks.title: Weekly digest: <=10 yes/no/other questions, SMTP or static page
tasks.description: Pick the top 10 pending proposals by impact (usage score from mining), render each as one short question with evidence and `yes / no / other` (Hebrew and English templates), as HTML+text email via smtplib (host/port/TLS from Settings) and as a static page written to disk; if SMTP is not configured or fails, only the page is produced and the failure is logged. Applying replies is out of scope tonight (only rendering and sending).
acceptance: renders golden HTML/text for 10 sample proposals in Hebrew (RTL markup) and English
an SMTP failure (stub server) falls back to the page without raising
never more than 10 questions; ordering is deterministic

tasks.title: Statistics collection: catalog first, sample fallback, quiet window
tasks.description: Schedule collection in the quiet window (default 21:00-07:00 Asia/Jerusalem, or Settings.quiet_windows when set). Read pg_stats and pg_class first; Oracle ALL_TAB_COL_STATISTICS, SQL Server stats DMVs and Elasticsearch index stats have parsers for the same shape. Fall back to a capped read when the catalog has nothing. Incremental: only new or resized partitions. Existence checks are SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1. Sentinel YAML is separate from the semantic layer. Context Pack and find_data append one short stats line for tables the question already matched. The linter rules in C19 consume the stored rows.
acceptance: noon in Asia/Jerusalem does not collect; 23:00 does; force overrides the clock
pg_stats rows become null share, distinct count and a complete distribution when the most-common values are the whole column
against live Postgres, planted NULL/0/''/whitespace shares match and a missing value is reported absent by the bounded lookup
an unrelated question's empty Context Pack does not gain a statistics dump
tasks.notes: The live Postgres check is tests/integration/test_stats_postgres.py --require-services. The unit command above covers the parsers, the window and the pack.

tasks.title: MCP server skeleton: 5 tools, health, auth hook
tasks.description: Using the installed MCP Python SDK (2.x: `from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer`; READ the installed package and https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io before coding: 1.x FastMCP examples found online are outdated), build an HTTP (streamable HTTP) server exposing 5 tools with pydantic input/output schemas: find_data, query, get_more, history, feedback (stubs returning a typed NOT_IMPLEMENTED result). Plus `GET /healthz` and `POST /context` (stub). Pluggable auth: a `TokenVerifier` interface; the dev implementation reads static tokens from a file and maps them to a user identity; identity reaches tool handlers through a request context object. `mdqm serve --host --port`. Tool descriptions are short and written for weak models (what it does, when to call it, one example).
acceptance: an in-process MCP client (SDK client over streamable HTTP on an ephemeral port) lists exactly 5 tools and calls each
missing/invalid token -> 401 and the tool handler is never reached
a valid token -> the handler sees the user identity
schemas for all tools are exported to docs/tool-schemas.json by a script and a test checks it is up to date
tasks.notes: Loopback needed: enable sockets for 127.0.0.1 in this test module only.

tasks.title: Tool find_data wired to the Context Pack
tasks.description: find_data(question, sources?) returns the Context Pack plus a proposed spec skeleton (from the best example or measure). Empty-search logging from H04. Output stays within the pack budget.
acceptance: through the in-process MCP client: a Hebrew question and an English question about credit limits return the same tables and measure
an unknown question returns an empty pack with a short hint, not an error

tasks.title: Tool query: lint, compile, plan, cache, execute, summarise (single source)
tasks.description: Orchestrate the whole path for one source: lint (C11) -> compile (C09) -> EXPLAIN gate (A03 or the fallback by capability) -> cache lookup (C14) -> governor + execute -> summary (C16) -> history (H03) and audit (H02). Response: status, summary, sample, result_handle, applied_fixes, freshness per segment, plan {partitions_scanned, index}, quality report, and a compact context pack on every error and (budget permitting) on success. `dry_run` stops after the plan; `fresh=true` bypasses the cache.
